title: A fair transition beyond suspended routines

captions.physics: Sharing responsibility according to actual conditions
captions.energy: Cancelling old routines before replacements exist

meaning: Your domestic agreement preserves support when ending the old includes clear temporary conditions instead of leaving both people indefinitely waiting for comfort.
text: You can arrange responsibility through fairness: recognising work, dividing manageable tasks and considering decisions’ consequences. Justice in the physical position of Muladhara describes these actions. Death in energy tests your footing through abruptly cancelling the old before its replacement is ready. The Hanged Man in emotions experiences familiar life suspended: the former has ended while the new cannot yet be used. A shared decision can therefore be fair in intention and demanding in practice when transition lacks clear arrangements and daily inconvenience seemingly counts as no part of the actual load.

For example, you remove an old hallway cupboard. New storage is still being chosen while belongings must be moved between rooms. **Transition also needs fairly shared conditions.** Temporary hooks and a clear place for bags do not cancel the new direction. They restore available life now, without meaningful change requiring silence and no support until a final choice that itself needs time and calm attention from two.

The difficulty is treating care for the temporary routine as insufficient decisiveness. Inconvenience preserves the transition’s purity while work stays invisible. Home looks renewing and feels stopped. An agreement helps more dependably when present action has value too, without a usable intermediate form first proving that you have permanently abandoned a more comfortable future answer.
